questions.q: In `nvidia-smi topo -m` output, which connection type is the fastest?
options: SYS
PHB
NVx (an NVLink connection)
PXB
questions.explain: NVx entries indicate a direct NVLink connection between two GPUs, the fastest connection type reported by nvidia-smi topo -m.

questions.q: What does a "SYS" connection type indicate between two GPUs?
options: A direct NVLink connection
The GPUs are connected through a single PCIe switch
The GPUs are on the same physical card
The connection crosses a NUMA/CPU socket boundary — the slowest listed path
questions.explain: SYS indicates the slowest connection type: the path crosses a NUMA or CPU socket boundary, often also traversing the CPU interconnect in addition to PCIe.

questions.q: What does the "CPU Affinity" column in nvidia-smi topo -m output tell you?
options: The CUDA Toolkit version compatible with that GPU
Which CPU cores are physically closest to a given GPU, useful for pinning CPU-side work like DataLoader workers
The maximum clock speed of the GPU
The number of NVLink connections available
questions.explain: CPU Affinity lists which CPU cores are physically closest (same NUMA node) to a given GPU, which matters for pinning CPU-side work to avoid cross-NUMA memory access penalties.

questions.q: Why might an 8-GPU server not scale much better than a 4-GPU server for a given training job?
options: Because 8-GPU servers never have NVLink
Because if half the GPUs are only connected via a slow SYS path, communication involving those GPUs can bottleneck the whole job
Because PyTorch only supports up to 4 GPUs per process group
Because NCCL cannot run on more than 4 GPUs
questions.explain: If some GPU pairs are connected via the slow SYS path (crossing NUMA/CPU boundaries) rather than NVLink, communication involving those GPUs becomes a bottleneck, limiting the overall scaling benefit of having more GPUs.

questions.q: Ordering the connection types from fastest to slowest, which is correct?
options: SYS, PHB, PXB, PIX, NVx
NVx, PIX, PXB, PHB, SYS
PHB, NVx, SYS, PIX, PXB
PIX, PXB, NVx, SYS, PHB
questions.explain: From fastest to slowest: NVx (direct NVLink), PIX (single PCIe switch), PXB (multiple PCIe switches), PHB (PCIe host bridge), and SYS (crosses a NUMA/CPU socket boundary, slowest).
